correctness.rationale: A basis of the tensor quotient modulo two-sided mutually zero products has at most one class per vertex and two per arrow: all radical-radical pairs and off-diagonal vertex pairs vanish, and two explicit zero-product tensor relations collapse the four endpoint tensors of each nonloop arrow. The product-pair map has exactly one dimension per vertex, two per nonloop arrow, and one per loop. Each loop provides a bilinear functional that vanishes whenever the first product vanishes, and its values on the two loop endpoint tensors distinguish it modulo product form. Independent loop classes meet the spanning bound, so the exact dimension and basis follow over every field. The included program exhaustively verifies twenty finite cases over the prime fields of orders two and three; generality depends on the algebraic argument, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The quotient of bilinear functionals satisfying two-sided zero-product vanishing by product-form functionals is canonical. Its complete determination by the number of quiver loops gives a sharp iff classification, a dimension and explicit obstruction basis, and a finite-field enumerator. The theorem covers oriented cycles of unbounded sizes, including infinite-global-dimension cases not reached by the motivating sufficient homological criterion. The data are naturally attached to first-order quiver self-extensions, not an artificial finite numerical slice.
